name: Claude Code on the web
operator: Anthropic (the vendor); each user is the operator of their own deployment
basis: the vendor’s own documentation and a published, measured deployment shape
what: The same coding agent in a cloud session: a managed container with one repository attached and a proxy above it.
note: An example scan of a product as its vendor documents it, not of any one deployment. Disclosure: the agent that wrote this scan runs on this product, in this shape.

grant.product: Claude Code on the web (a remote session container)
grant.statement: This describes a published deployment shape. It is not an assessment, an audit, a certification or a security review of any named product, and it carries no adjective and no score.

I04.n: It runs Claude Code sessions in a cloud virtual machine.

I08.n: It clones the repository, makes changes and pushes branches.

I10.n: The repository, the shell and the code host.

I11.n: Sessions reach package registries and other allowlisted domains.

I18.n: In Accept edits, which the permission modes page says corresponds to the default mode in cloud sessions, Claude makes changes and pushes a branch without stopping for approval; the person reviews the result The permission modes page adds that Accept edits corresponds to the default mode in cloud sessions.
I18.span: Claude makes changes and pushes a branch without stopping for approval

I20.n: The vendor states what cloud sessions are for.

I21.n: A cloud environment sets network access, variables and a setup script.

I23.n: A published deployment shape, measured on one operator’s configured session, lists 15 capabilities, 13 of them observed; its rows include that operator’s commit hooks and the session’s registered signing identity.

I25.n: GitHub credentials never enter the session’s machine; a proxy attaches them on the server.

I46.n: Two capabilities in the published shape are limited by a setting: repository writes by the clone’s commit hooks (observed) and scheduled tasks by the operator’s own list (self-reported).

I61.n: The model configuration page lists the models Claude Code uses by alias and the version each resolves to per provider; cloud sessions take the same /model command.
I61.span: Uses the latest Opus model for complex reasoning tasks

I63.n: The vendor points to a SOC 2 Type 2 report and an ISO 27001 certificate at its trust centre; they cover the vendor, not a user’s deployment.

I12.n: The cloud page says agent teams are off by default and are enabled with an environment variable; the agent teams page describes instances, each in its own context, that message each other.
I12.span: Agent teams are off by default but can be enabled

S3.n: The documentation publishes an llms.txt index.

I56.n: By default its commits, including commits from cloud sessions, carry a Co-Authored-By trailer naming the Claude model in use; a setting can change or hide it.

I58.n: A page describes what data is sent, kept and used.

I45.n: With the default (Trusted) network access, sessions reach package registries and allowlisted domains "and nothing else through the session’s network"; the page describes Anthropic's agent proxy, outside the session's VM, handling the session's outbound requests.
I45.span: and nothing else through the session’s network

findings.finding: Same as the local scan: the overview names the product but I found no model listed on it. Cite the page that lists models or remove.

"Work arrives as a branch for a person to review" is not a statement that a person must approve a high-impact action. The page (Review changes) shows that review is possible; it does not say a push or any other action waits for approval. Re-read against the indicator and cite the sentence, or lower the credit.

The note says the person starts a task and reviews the result. The page also says the person picks a permission mode for a cloud session, so how independent it is depends on that mode, and the answer names no mode. State which mode the default is, from the page, or mark the mode as chosen by the person.

The source says a network secret is added by the proxy to requests for the hosts the operator lists. That shows a key is attached for listed hosts; it does not show that tokens are bound to the service they were issued for. The indicator needs the operation, so documented does not count, and the claim is a stretch from the sentence. Consider removing.

The cited source is the local product's agent-teams page. The cloud page says in its own words that agent teams are off by default and can be enabled with an environment variable. Cite the cloud page, which also gives the configuration the answer needs.

The profile's description says its grant was measured on this site's own agent environment ("the mandate hook and the insurance policy"; signing key "registered as an agent identity in this site's registry"). That is one operator's configured session, not the product as shipped. The counts in the note are right (15 rows, 13 observed). Say in the note that the measured shape includes that operator's hooks and identity.

The note is right: two rows have barrier "setting" (write.repository.tenant, create.schedule.tenant). The grade could be observed for one of them, which was observed on the thing itself; one is self-reported. Leave as it is or say which.

The span "and nothing else through the session's network" (7 words) is in the cloud environments page. The scope says read from a measured grant only; the grant has send.endpoint.allowed as a boundary, observed. The credit should come from the grant. Check how the scorer treats it.

Opened each source. The note matches the page; grade and mode are right. I25 matches "your GitHub credentials stay encrypted on Anthropic's servers and never enter a session's VM". I11 is correctly the default because the Trusted level reaches allowlisted domains.

Argued against Autonomy 4, which here is I10 (default), I18 (default) and, under the corrected rule, no S1. The new I18 source is right and the span is exact: on the web quickstart, "Accept edits: Claude makes changes and pushes a branch without stopping for approval", with Auto (a classifier reviews) and Plan (waits for approval of an approach before editing) beside it, and "Cloud sessions don't offer Manual or Bypass permissions". I confirmed the claim the note adds on the permission modes page: "Accept edits corresponds to default mode: cloud sessions pre-approve file edits regardless of mode". That sentence is not on the page the answer cites; the answer should cite the permission modes page as well, or the note should say where it comes from. Against the level: in the default mode nobody approves anything before the push, so "the person approves critical decisions only" holds only because the critical decision, merging, is outside the session. The note says the person reviews the result; that is on the web page (Review changes), and I accept it as the basis.

Same argument as Replit and Manus. "The repository, the shell and the code host" is three parts of one coding task. The rule counts it, and Autonomy 4 follows from it with I18; nothing cited shows a multi-step workflow across systems. Condition for sign-off: the card says A3 is the level evidenced by actions and that A4 rests on a count of reached systems, as it does on the other cards. This is a rule matter, already with gamma-ray@.

Under the corrected rule (Spectrum 0.2) Autonomy 3 needs no S1, and this card has none: no source names a customer or gives usage for cloud sessions. The card therefore reads Acts and Orchestrates with no public evidence of anyone using it. That is the rule, not this scan, and the "in production" badge is not shown. I do not object; the card should not word A3 as in production.

Round one finding repeated from the local scan: the note says pull request descriptions get "a Generated with Claude Code line". The settings reference says "pull request descriptions get plain text" and gives no wording. Remove the wording. The commit trailer is on the page ("Default: unset, so Claude Code adds Co-Authored-By"), and the span is the page's sentence about the name of the model, which does not by itself say AI; use the trailer sentence.

Restored under the Spectrum reading. The note does not say what enforces the limit, which that reading asks for ("say in the note what enforces it"). The source says the session's network reaches package registries and allowlisted domains and "nothing else"; the cloud environments page names the proxies that enforce it. Name it. No effect on any level here (Control is below 1).

Removed in answer to round one, with reasons that match the pages: a push does not wait for a person, and a key attached for listed hosts is not a token bound to its service. Control falls to none; that is right on this evidence.
Re-sourced to the cloud page. Span "Agent teams are off by default but can be enabled" is exact (10 words), mode available (teams). Round one finding answered.

I61: model configuration page, span exact. I23: the note now says the measured shape is one operator's configured session with its commit hooks and signing identity; I checked it against the profile. I46: names which row is observed and which self-reported. All answered.

Levels three and four: Autonomy 4 only. Reach 2, Openness 2, Control none are below three. Verdict pass, on the conditions that the I56 wording is removed, the I18 note cites its second page and the card names the configurations (it does).
